# Previews: next steps

Generated by `maul setup previews` (maul v0.12.40) for the **gateway TLS on a LoadBalancer** recipe on **aks**.
Previews will be served at `https://<project>-<issue>.acme-previews.dev`, and viewers sign in at `https://preview-auth.maul.acme.dev`.
Nothing here has been applied: run the steps below in order. Running `maul setup previews` again shows what would
change before it replaces a file, and never draws a new Dex client secret unless you pass
`--rotate dex-client-secret`.

`maul setup previews -n maul --apply --values <your values> --chart-version <version>` runs the in-cluster
steps below for you, in order, with your kubeconfig and helm, stopping at the first failure (add `--dry-run` to list
them first). Preview nodes, image pulls, Dex's static client, the DNS records stay yours.

## Files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT-STEPS.md` | This file. |
| `answers.yaml` | Every answer, the edge and the CLI version: a re-run starts from it. No secret. |
| `manifests/certificate.yaml` | The cert-manager Certificate for `*.<suffix>` and the sign-in host. |
| `manifests/issuer.yaml` | The ACME Issuer that answers the Certificate's DNS-01 challenge (a ClusterIssuer when cert-manager's own identity answers). |
| `maul-previews.values.yaml` | maul's chart values for previews, layered after your own. |
| `secrets/dex-maul-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml` | The same secret, in Dex's namespace, for its static client (0600). |
| `secrets/maul-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml` | The relay's Dex client secret, in the release namespace (0600). |
| `secrets/preview-dns01-credentials.secret.yaml` | The DNS-01 solver's credential, in the release namespace (0600). |
| `upstream/cert-manager.values.yaml` | cert-manager's values, for the chart version maul pins (v1.21.2). |

The files under `secrets/` (mode 0600) hold the only copy of the Dex client secret and of
the DNS credential you gave. Apply them, or encrypt them (sops,
sealed-secrets) before they go anywhere else; never commit them as they are.

## 1. Before you start

- maul is installed in namespace `maul` as release `maul`, with `intentController.enabled: true`
  in your values: previews are built for intents, and the preview-controller needs intent-controller.
- NetworkPolicy is enforced. On AKS, the network policy engine (Azure, Calico or Cilium) is chosen when the cluster is created: check `networkProfile.networkPolicy` is not none.
- cert-manager is installed in step 5 from `upstream/cert-manager.values.yaml` (chart v1.21.2),
  unless it already runs: then run the command again with `--cert-manager-installed`.

## 2. Preview nodes

Every slot Pod selects `maul.run/previews=true` and tolerates the taint `maul.run/preview-only=true:NoExecute`. Add at least one node with both, set when it registers so no other Pod lands on it first.

```sh
az aks nodepool add --resource-group <group> --cluster-name <cluster> --name previews \
  --labels maul.run/previews=true --node-taints maul.run/preview-only=true:NoExecute
```

`maul-previews.values.yaml` sets `preview.nodeIsolation` over your own values, but Helm merges its `selector` map: remove any `preview.nodeIsolation.selector` from your own values, or Pods require those labels too.

## 3. Preview image pulls

Preview images are `acme.azurecr.io/acme/maul/previews/<app>:sha-<commit>`. Slot Pods may not reference a Secret, so pulls are
the node's own: give the preview node pool's kubelet identity AcrPull on the repository holding `acme/maul/previews/*` only.

## 4. Dex

Add the relay's static client to Dex's configuration, with its one redirect URI:

```yaml
staticClients:
  - id: maul-preview-auth
    name: maul previews
    secretEnv: MAUL_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
    redirectURIs:
      - https://preview-auth.maul.acme.dev/dex/callback
```

Give Dex the secret in that environment variable from the Secret in its namespace (with Dex's Helm chart:
`envVars: [{name: MAUL_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: maul-preview-auth-client, key: clientSecret}}}]`),
then roll Dex:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/dex-maul-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml
```

## 5. TLS

The gateway terminates TLS itself with one certificate for `*.acme-previews.dev` and `preview-auth.maul.acme.dev`, issued by cert-manager
and picked up again at every renewal without a restart.

Install cert-manager at the version maul pins:

```sh
helm upgrade --install cert-manager cert-manager --repo https://charts.jetstack.io \
  --version v1.21.2 -n cert-manager --create-namespace -f upstream/cert-manager.values.yaml
```

The Issuer answers the challenge with the `azure` DNS-01 solver. Give the solver's identity `DNS Zone Contributor` on only the DNS zones holding `acme-previews.dev` and `preview-auth.maul.acme.dev`, never on the resource group or the subscription.

Its credential is in `secrets/preview-dns01-credentials.secret.yaml`:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/preview-dns01-credentials.secret.yaml
```

```sh
kubectl apply -f manifests/issuer.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/certificate.yaml
kubectl -n maul wait certificate/preview-wildcard --for=condition=Ready --timeout=10m
```

`previewAuth.gateway.tls.secrets` names its Secret, `preview-wildcard-tls`. The two names sit on different
registrable domains, so usually in two DNS zones: the solver must be able to answer for both.

## 6. Install

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/maul-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml
helm upgrade maul oci://ghcr.io/devthenet-labs/maul/charts/maul -n maul --version 0.12.40 \
  -f <your values> -f maul-previews.values.yaml
```

One upgrade: the gateway needs no permit stage. `previewController.config.apiServerCIDR: auto` is looked up at render time, so it needs `helm upgrade` against the cluster (not
`helm template` or a GitOps render, which must set the kubernetes Service's `/32` instead).

## 7. DNS

Point two records at the edge's address:

- `*.acme-previews.dev`
- `preview-auth.maul.acme.dev`

The address is the gateway's own load balancer (`kubectl -n maul get service maul-preview-gateway -o
jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0]}'` once it is provisioned).
`externalTrafficPolicy: Local` keeps the viewer's address as the gateway's peer, so
`previewAuth.gateway.forwardedHops` is 0.

## 8. Check

```sh
maul check previews -n maul
```

Every line should PASS before the first intent's preview is opened.

## Rolling back

In reverse order, all by deletion:

1. Set `previewAuth.gateway.enabled: false` (or `preview.enabled: false`) and run the same `helm upgrade`.
2. `kubectl delete -f manifests/certificate.yaml` and `kubectl delete -f manifests/issuer.yaml`.
3. Remove the two DNS records.
4. Remove the static client from Dex, and delete the Secrets (`kubectl delete -f secrets/`).
   Uninstall what this recipe installed if nothing else uses it: `helm uninstall cert-manager -n cert-manager` (its CRDs stay, and
   with them every Certificate in the cluster).
5. Delete what the chart keeps on uninstall, as `docs/intents/preview-sign-in.md` lists it.
